author: EmuCore - Hub
title: How to fix screen shaking (interlacing) in PCSX2: PS2 Emulation
summary: Mr. Sujano isolates interlacing as a common cause of vertical screen shake in PCSX2 and demonstrates a targeted correction path, while pointing viewers toward game-specific no-interlacing codes instead of promising one universal display switch.

blocks.text: This compact troubleshooting video begins with a recognizable symptom: an image that appears to vibrate vertically even though the game is otherwise running. It connects that behavior to the interlaced output expected by many PlayStation 2 titles, then shows the PCSX2 controls used to test a cleaner presentation. The linked forum thread adds game-specific no-interlacing codes, which matters because a patch can change how a title produces frames rather than merely altering the emulator window after rendering.

Screen shake, tearing, unstable frame pacing and texture shimmer can look similar in a compressed recording but have different causes. The upload does not identify every game, PCSX2 build, renderer or video mode for which its recommendation was tested, and a no-interlacing code may be revision-specific. Treat the demonstration as a diagnosis branch: compare the same static scene, preserve per-game settings, confirm the disc serial, and undo the change if cutscenes, field order or timing becomes worse.
